source_meta._title: Some words within "/clear" command feedback messages are always pluralized

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3 client in a single-player world, using the English (US) language and with commands/cheats enabled. No specific seed, coordinates, dimension, game mode, item, entity, or multiplayer server is required.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected release Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3 rather than a listed fix version.
Use the vanilla English (US) language resources; disable any resource pack that replaces English command translations.
Have permission to execute /tellraw. For the single-player procedure below, create or open a world with cheats enabled.
Use the report-supplied tellraw command without adding translation arguments or changing its JSON syntax.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition 1.19.3, and launch the game. Do not use a later version for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Options, select Language, choose English (US), confirm the selection, and return to the title screen. If English (US) is already selected, leave it selected.
steps.success_cue: The menus are displayed in English and English (US) is the selected language.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and create a new world. Use Creative mode as a simple way to establish a command-capable test environment, and ensure Allow Cheats is set to ON before selecting Create New World. An existing cheats-enabled world may be used instead because the report does not require fresh world data.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a loaded single-player world and is permitted to run commands.

steps.action: Wait before executing the test until surrounding terrain has rendered and normal player movement responds without world-loading interruption.
steps.success_cue: Terrain is visible around the player and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press the control bound to Open Chat, which is T by default, to place the text cursor in the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report-supplied tellraw command using the affected translation key commands.clear.success.single. Include the leading slash, preserve the capitalization and JSON punctuation exactly, and press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: A new tellraw message is rendered for the player without a red command-syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Immediately press the Open Chat control again so the recent tellraw message remains fully visible in expanded chat. Do not enter another command or clear the chat.
steps.success_cue: Expanded chat is open and the tellraw message produced by step 6 is visible as the most recent chat entry.

stor.handoff_condition: The translation component for commands.clear.success.single has just been rendered by the report-supplied /tellraw command, and expanded chat is open with that message visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the wording of the rendered message.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world seed, coordinates, dimension, or server type. The plan uses a Creative single-player world with cheats enabled solely as the simplest command-capable environment.

The report permits any of four affected translation keys. This minimal deterministic plan uses commands.clear.success.single; the other listed keys can be tested independently by replacing only that key in the otherwise identical command.
The supplied command does not provide values for the translation string's substitution fields. This plan preserves the command exactly instead of inventing additional translation arguments.

source_meta._title: Fast graphics description is slightly misleading

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 client; local singleplayer Creative-mode world; English (US) language; default resource pack; no graphics-altering mods, shaders, or custom resource packs.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 is installed and can be selected as a separate launcher installation.
The executor can create and enter a local singleplayer world.
Use a mouse and keyboard, or equivalent bound controls, that can left-click menu buttons and hold the pointer stationary over a button.
Keep the window large enough that the complete Video Settings screen and its tooltips can be displayed.
Do not use mods, shaders, or resource packs that alter block rendering or option text.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that uses Java Edition version 1.18.1, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as 1.18.1.

steps.action: Set the game language to English (US) so the English graphics tooltip cited by the report is used. From the main menu, open Options, select Language, choose English (US), and click Done.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu and option labels are displayed in English.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select Create New World, change Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. No particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins for a new Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Wait without opening another menu until terrain has rendered around the player and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move and look around normally, with nearby terrain fully rendered.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab and search one at a time for Oak Leaves, Ice, White Stained Glass, Slime Block, and Honey Block. Place one stack of each item into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the inventory and game screen.
steps.exact_input: oak leaves; ice; white stained glass; slime block; honey block
steps.success_cue: Oak Leaves, Ice, White Stained Glass, Slime Block, and Honey Block are present in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Press E to close the inventory. In an open, well-lit location, select each prepared hotbar item in turn and right-click the ground or an existing block face to place one sample of each block in a horizontal row. Leave enough space and choose a viewing angle that allows the player to see a face of every sample, preferably with open sky or distant terrain behind them.
steps.success_cue: A row containing Oak Leaves, Ice, White Stained Glass, a Slime Block, and a Honey Block is placed and visible.

steps.action: Position the player several blocks in front of the row and aim the camera so all five block samples are simultaneously visible. Avoid changing this viewing position unnecessarily during the graphics comparison.
steps.success_cue: All five test blocks are within the current view and their chunks are fully rendered.

steps.action: Press Esc, click Options, and click Video Settings. Find the button whose label begins with Graphics. If it is not already set to Fancy, left-click it repeatedly until its complete label reads Graphics: Fancy; the option may cycle through more than two graphics modes.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen is open and the graphics button reads Graphics: Fancy.

steps.action: Return to the world by clicking Done on the Video Settings screen, clicking Done on the Options screen, and clicking Back to Game on the pause menu. Look at the prepared block row once to establish the pre-Fast rendering reference without moving or replacing the blocks.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed with all five prepared blocks visible while Graphics remains set to Fancy.

steps.action: Press Esc, click Options, and click Video Settings again.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen is open and its option buttons are responsive.

steps.action: Locate the Graphics button in the Video Settings screen. Confirm that this is the button currently labeled Graphics: Fancy before changing it.
steps.success_cue: The cursor can be positioned over the Graphics button and the button currently identifies the Fancy setting.

steps.action: Left-click the Graphics button as many times as necessary until its label reads Graphics: Fast. Stop clicking as soon as Fast is selected.
steps.success_cue: The graphics button visibly reads Graphics: Fast.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer away from the Graphics button, then place it over the Graphics: Fast button and keep it stationary until the graphics-setting tooltip panel appears. Do not change the setting while the tooltip is displayed.
steps.success_cue: A tooltip panel is visible for the Graphics: Fast button, and the button still reads Graphics: Fast.

steps.action: Exit the settings menus by clicking Done on the Video Settings screen, clicking Done on the Options screen, and clicking Back to Game on the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The player has returned to gameplay with Graphics still set to Fast.

steps.action: Face the previously prepared row from approximately the same position and viewing angle used under Fancy. Keep the view steady until the Oak Leaves, Ice, White Stained Glass, Slime Block, and Honey Block have all rendered under the Fast setting.
steps.success_cue: All five prepared block types are simultaneously visible, surrounding chunks are loaded, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Press Esc, open Options, and open Video Settings one final time so the text-related trigger can be presented to the observation subsystem after the rendering comparison setup has been completed.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen is open again.

steps.action: Verify that the Graphics button still reads Graphics: Fast. If another value is shown, left-click the button until Fast is restored.
steps.success_cue: The graphics button reads Graphics: Fast.

steps.action: Move the pointer off the Graphics button, then place it over Graphics: Fast and hold the pointer stationary until the tooltip is fully visible. Leave the cursor and menu unchanged for the observation handoff.
steps.success_cue: The Graphics: Fast tooltip is fully visible and remains on screen without the cursor moving.

stor.handoff_condition: Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1 is displaying the Video Settings screen with Graphics set to Fast, the cursor is stationary over that button, and its tooltip is fully visible. The prepared leaf and comparison-block row has already been rendered once under Fancy and once under Fast. Begin observation while the tooltip remains visible.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required world seed, terrain location, or game mode. A new Creative-mode world and manually placed test blocks are used only to make the rendering comparison deterministic.
The report does not explicitly specify the game language. English (US) is selected because the report provides an English translation string and wording is the subject of the issue.

The formal reproduction steps identify leaves but do not define an exhaustive set of other block families to test. Ice, stained glass, slime blocks, and honey blocks are included as representative comparisons because the report discusses them, but this selection alone is not an exhaustive survey of every block.
The exact delay before the tooltip appears can depend on input timing; the executable condition is to keep the cursor stationary until the tooltip is visible.

The final reopening and re-hovering of the Graphics button repeats the report's tooltip action so the observation subsystem receives the game in the exact text-trigger state rather than after the menu has been closed.

source_meta._title: Gamerule description strings within the world creation menu consist of inconsistent concluding punctuation

stor.environment: Local single-player Java Edition world using the integrated server, with the client language set to English (US), chat visible, and commands enabled. Use Creative mode as a practical way to ensure commands are available. No specific seed, coordinates, dimension, world type, or graphics settings are required.
preconditions: Install and launch the unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.4 client, which the report explicitly lists as affected.
Set the game language to English (US) so the translation keys render as the English descriptions quoted by the report.
Have a single-player world available in which the player can execute permission-level commands. For a new test world, using Creative mode with commands allowed is the simplest setup.
Ensure chat messages are visible rather than hidden.

Use the two representative translation keys in this plan as a deterministic comparison: gamerule.forgiveDeadPlayers.description is from the report's group whose displayed text ends with punctuation, while gamerule.doLimitedCrafting.description is from the group whose displayed text is listed without concluding punctuation.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for version 1.19.4, and launch the game. Do not use 1.20 Pre-release 1 or a later version because the report identifies 1.20 Pre-release 1 as the fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is open and the displayed version is 1.19.4.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Language, select English (US), and confirm the selection with Done. Return to the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The menus are displayed in English (US), and the main menu is visible again.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer. Either open an existing disposable world with commands enabled or select Create New World and configure a disposable test world. If creating a world, select Creative game mode and ensure commands are allowed, then create the world. The world name and seed do not matter.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a world in which in-game commands can be executed.

steps.action: Wait before entering commands. Continue only after the terrain around the player has rendered and normal movement responds without world-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are rendered and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default. Type the report's tellraw command using gamerule.forgiveDeadPlayers.description as the translation key. Include the leading slash, preserve capitalization, and do not add spaces inside the JSON value.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is present in the chat input field and has not yet been executed.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command. Do not clear the chat afterward.
steps.success_cue: A translated gamerule-description message has appeared in the player's chat overlay.

steps.action: Press T again to reopen chat. Type the same tellraw command, this time replacing the translation key with gamerule.doLimitedCrafting.description. Include the leading slash and enter the command exactly as shown.
steps.success_cue: The second complete command is present in the chat input field and has not yet been executed.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the second command. Stop issuing commands and leave the chat messages visible for inspection.
steps.success_cue: The second translated gamerule-description message has appeared, and both representative description messages are available in the chat history for end-of-string inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The two representative gamerule description translation keys have just been rendered in English through separate /tellraw commands, with the chat history still visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect and compare the concluding characters of the two displayed strings.
uncertainties: The title and description characterize the affected strings as being within the world creation menu, but the report's formal reproduction procedure displays the same translation keys through /tellraw. This plan preserves and operationalizes the command-based procedure rather than substituting a direct world-creation-menu procedure.

The report says that any listed affected string can be displayed. Using one key from each punctuation group is a practical deterministic choice so that the relevant strings can be compared without executing every key in the table.

Creative mode and a new disposable single-player world are not stated as requirements by the report; they are practical setup choices for obtaining permission to execute /tellraw. Any environment in which the player can successfully execute that command should be equivalent for this reproduction route.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-211071:Some words within "/spreadplayers" command feedback messages are always pluralized
source_meta._title: Some words within "/function" and "/schedule" command feedback messages are always pluralized

stor.environment: A local singleplayer world running Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3, with the game language set to English (US) and commands/cheats enabled. Creative mode is recommended only as the simplest way to prepare a disposable command-enabled test world; the report does not require a particular game mode, seed, coordinates, dimension, or server type.
preconditions: Use an affected Java Edition version. Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3 is recommended because it is a stable release explicitly listed in the report's affected versions; 1.19.2 and snapshot 22w45a are also listed as affected.
Set the game language to English (US) so the displayed translation matches the English text documented in the report.
Load a singleplayer world in which the player is permitted to execute commands. For a new disposable test world, selecting Creative mode and enabling cheats is a practical setup choice.
No datapack, resource pack, specific seed, coordinates, structure, item, entity, or dimension is required.
Keep the in-game chat display visible after executing the command so the separate observation subsystem can inspect the generated translated message.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation for Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3, and start the game. Do not use a newer version for this reproduction run.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is visible and identifies the running version as 1.19.3.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Options, then Language, select English (US), and confirm the selection by pressing Done until you return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen interface is displayed in English and English (US) is the selected language.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a disposable world with commands enabled. Creative mode is recommended for convenience. If the world-creation screen exposes a separate Allow Cheats setting, set it to ON before creating the world. An existing command-enabled world may be used instead.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a singleplayer world in which commands can be executed.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before opening chat. Continue only after nearby terrain is rendered and normal player movement responds without a loading pause.
steps.success_cue: The world is fully interactive, nearby chunks are visible, and player controls respond normally.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to open the in-game chat input field.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open at the bottom of the screen and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report-provided tellraw command with XYZ replaced by the affected translation key commands.schedule.created.function. Include the leading slash and preserve the JSON punctuation and quotation marks exactly.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is present in the chat input field with no added spaces or missing quotation marks, braces, colon, slash, or translation-key segments.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command. Do not run additional commands or close the chat display after the translated line appears.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and one translated tellraw message beginning with the wording for scheduling a function appears in the player's chat display. Because the supplied report command provides no translation arguments, substitution placeholders may remain visible; leave the resulting line unchanged for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The /tellraw command using the commands.schedule.created.function translation key has just been executed successfully, and the resulting translated message is visible in the English (US) in-game chat. Hand control to the observation subsystem before entering another command or closing the chat display.
uncertainties: The report permits any listed affected translation key rather than requiring a particular one. This plan selects commands.schedule.created.function as one concrete, deterministic example and does not imply that it is the only affected key.

The report does not specify a game mode, seed, dimension, coordinates, or whether to use singleplayer or multiplayer. A disposable Creative singleplayer world with cheats enabled is a practical execution choice, not a claimed bug requirement.

The report's supplied /tellraw command does not provide values for the translation string's substitution placeholders. The plan preserves that command exactly except for replacing XYZ with the selected translation key, as instructed by the report; placeholder rendering may therefore remain literal or otherwise indicate absent arguments.

The report discusses multiple affected translation keys, but its reproduction instructions explicitly say to display any one of them. This minimum plan executes one affected key once and hands off immediately, avoiding unnecessary repeated messages.

source_meta._title: Debug key binds text is improperly capitalized

stor.environment: Vanilla single-player Minecraft Java Edition 25w41a with the language set to English (US), default resources, and commands/cheats enabled. No specific game mode, seed, coordinates, server, or additional player is required.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and start snapshot 25w41a; enable snapshot installations in the launcher if necessary.
Use the affected version 25w41a rather than fix version 25w43a or a later release.
Use the built-in English (US) language so the English capitalization listed in the report is displayed.
Use a world in which the executing player has permission to run /tellraw, such as a single-player world created with Allow Commands enabled.
Disable custom resource packs that replace the affected English translation strings.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create a Java Edition installation that uses snapshot 25w41a, and launch it.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and identifies its version as 25w41a.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Options, select Language, choose English (US), and confirm with Done. If English (US) is already selected, leave it selected and return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen menus are displayed in English and English (US) is the active language.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new test world. In the world-creation settings, enable Allow Commands. Any game mode, world seed, and world-generation settings may be used because the report specifies none. Start the world.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a single-player world in which commands are permitted.

steps.action: Wait until the world has finished loading: surrounding terrain should be rendered and normal player movement should respond without a loading pause.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally and the nearby terrain is rendered.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Type the report's /tellraw command, replacing XYZ with one affected translation key. For a deterministic single-string reproduction, use the first listed key, key.debug.clearChat. Include the leading slash, and do not submit the command yet.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input field with no omitted characters.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error, and one translated text line is rendered in the chat/HUD for the executing player.

stor.handoff_condition: The /tellraw command using key.debug.clearChat has just executed successfully, and the resulting translated text line is currently visible for capitalization inspection.
uncertainties: The report permits any affected translation key and does not identify one mandatory key. This plan selects key.debug.clearChat, the first key in the report, as the simplest deterministic example.
The report does not explicitly state the active language. English (US) is selected as a practical requirement because the supplied current and expected strings are English strings.

The report does not specify game mode, seed, coordinates, or whether to use single-player or a server. A command-enabled single-player world is the minimum deterministic environment supported by the supplied reproduction.

To inspect another listed string, the same trigger can be repeated after handoff by replacing only key.debug.clearChat with that string's exact translation key; the report does not require every listed key to be tested in one run.
